instagram_caption:
Why did Disney let Tim Burton go over a dog? 🐶

In 1984 Burton, a young Disney animator, made Frankenweenie: a black-and-white short about a boy who revives his dead pet.

It was rated PG, which reportedly scrapped the plan to show it with Pinocchio. Burton says the ratings board told him, "There's nothing you can cut. It's just the tone."

Disney shelved it and Burton moved on, though he describes it as a parting of ways. Paul Reubens had seen the short, and Burton went on to direct Pee-wee's Big Adventure.

In 2012 Disney released his feature-length stop-motion remake, still black and white, still PG.
